cards.b: About 50 minutes including 6 minutes' transfer time, 40 marks, 25%. Multiple choice and matching; each text played twice.
1 hour, 45 marks, 25%. Six question groups: matching, multiple choice, and short answers in German.
About 10 minutes (plus 10 minutes' preparation), 40 marks, 25%. One role play and two topic conversations.
1 hour, 45 marks, 25%. Q1 form (5), Q2 directed writing (12), Q3 extended writing (28).
None: all candidates take the same four papers and can get grades A* to G.
Five answers, 2 marks each: communicated clearly with appropriate, accurate language. Minor errors allowed.
About four minutes each. Marked out of 15 for Communication and 15 for Quality of Language, across both.
Directed writing, about 80–90 words, 12 marks, on a familiar everyday topic.
Choose an email/letter or an article/blog, about 130–140 words, 28 marks.
Longer email/blog/article texts. Answer the questions with short answers in German; marked on understanding.
Everyday activities: time, food and drink, the human body and health, travel and transport.
Personal and social life: self, family and friends, home, colours, clothes, leisure time.
The world around us: people and places, nature, weather, technology, built environment, shopping.
The world of work: education (school, subjects) and work (jobs, careers, the workplace).
The international world: countries, nationalities, languages; culture, customs, faiths, celebrations.
Indirect speech (Konjunktiv I) and the passive: you need to understand them, not write them.

short.q: Explain what the examiner is looking for in the Speaking topic conversations.
short.model: Communication: relevant answers with developed, justified opinions. Quality of Language: a wide range of structures and vocabulary, accuracy, pronunciation and fluency.
points: Quality of Language: range and accuracy of structures

short.q: How should you use the time before each recording in Paper 1?
short.model: Read the options, underline key words, and predict the kind of answer (numbers, times, reasons). Watch for corrections such as nicht ... sondern.
points: Reads the options and finds key words

short.q: A Reading question asks for a short answer in German. How do you write it?
short.model: Find the part of the text that answers exactly the question, and write a short, clear German answer with the key detail, without copying irrelevant or wrong information.
points: Keeps the key detail clear in German

short.q: What should you do in the 10 minutes' preparation for the role play?
short.model: Read the card carefully, work out the situation and who you speak to (du or Sie), and prepare a full polite sentence for each prompt. You may not make notes.
points: Plans full, appropriate sentences without notes

short.q: Plan a Writing Q3 email about your last holiday: which tenses and structures would you include?
short.model: Perfect and imperfect for what you did and what it was like, an opinion with weil, a future or conditional (Nächstes Jahr werde ich ... / Ich würde gern ...), and linked sentences.
points: Opinion with a reason and a future or conditional
